answer: When actions arrive as a Poisson process, the gaps between them follow a known distribution; a human session fits it loosely, while a scripted farm shows gaps that are too regular or too clustered. The network fits the inter-arrival distribution per account and measures deviation from the fitted model, so a Sybil that replays identical timing across many accounts is exposed by its own regularity. Without this check, a harbor of fake sessions could flood the network overnight. When the ledge settles over the gale, the session holds because every action carried its own proof.
